evidence:
Scope and authority: inspected the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl, Quality Checks row 36 (#35) and Internal Quality Checks row 36 (#35). Both require defining behavior and durable server-backed state; the public row explicitly distinguishes server backing from same-origin. Applied frozen harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md, references/quality-checks.md:145-147, the staged contract's test.sh/restart sections, deterministic-checks.md's canonical-shared-files and verifier-contract guidance, and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md. All 50 frozen task-file hashes and all 34 frozen rule-file hashes matched manifest.json. Paths below prefixed task/ are under .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/.

The core execution and browser/server persistence legs are well specified. task/tests/gates/render/judge.toml:25 requires a new authored marker to appear in BOTH rendered preview and console after actual Run; hardcoded samples/editor text do not suffice. task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:49 and :56 separately grade filename-selected JS/HTML execution and CSS applied to the last successful document. task/tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25 requires an observed successful UI write and recorded identity/title/filename/exact source. Its :27 requires an independent clean context without copied browser storage, actual server-supplied data, and a reload/readback; it expressly accepts server-rendered documents without a JSON endpoint. task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:397-400 and judge.toml:343 additionally require two distinct saved records and exact reload fidelity. Static data, an unsaved buffer, localStorage-only state, or an unchanged success toast cannot satisfy these described probes. No re-authentication is required because instruction.md and app_context.md explicitly specify no accounts.

Confirmed defect: required process durability can receive a false-positive observation from the inherited restart helper. task/environment/instructions/integration.md:7 promises saved snippets, identities and revisions survive 'a complete process restart over the same database.' task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:409-415 prepares two ordinary saved records (including an advanced revision), calls restart_app once, then reads them and independently tests another write. judge.toml:350 assigns weight 2.00 to process durability, and :357 separately grades writing after the same completed restart. However task/tests/test.sh:152-159 sends SIGTERM and polls only for a bounded period, then proceeds even if the old process group remains alive. Lines 160-183 start a replacement, overwrite app.pid, and accept any successful HTTP probe; they never establish old-process termination or new-process liveness. task/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:45-47 then translates helper exit 0 into 'restart complete: the server was relaunched on the same database and answers HTTP'. Thus the required destructive state transition need not occur. This is an inherited canonical conflict, not task-author customization: task/tests/test.sh is byte-identical to frozen rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/test.sh, SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa.

Runtime confirmation: independently read the raw reproduction source qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-09-30/reproduce_restart.py and raw qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-repair3/inherited-restart-counterexample.json, rather than any reviewer report. The source creates a SIGTERM-resistant Node listener, extracts the unchanged heredoc helper, executes it, and records process identity before/after. Verified their SHA256s against raw-evidence-index.json: ef6d94b64ff5635e0e1fb69e5eaefea9e0d83cbe2004714c2510e7aa163c164a and 552bf6e7afa7707d093667e2e2d35fe8bbd88b54deedd73a401d22586fcc2e98. Recomputed frozen helper hash 0db23e8c7c8d70c7e934c4d13ccbb2326a4da2cb47f1b2ba1967009d829be3b7 matches the reproduction. Raw output records helper_returncode=0, old_pid=7, claimed_new_pid=67, old_still_running=true, after.pid=7, and replacement log 'EADDRINUSE' followed by 'app-restart pid=67 ready=1'. That directly confirms false restart success. No new Docker run or provider call was made for this review.

Positive evidence is preserved: hash-verified golden RESULTS.json (ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09) includes observed JS/HTML output, CSS color/background, exact Alpha/Beta reload readbacks, restart Primary id 5 revision 2 and Second id 6 revision 1 retained, and a later Primary revision 3 write. All recorded actual_app_files hashes match this frozen golden source. Relevant copied driver hashes also match RESULTS.json. The executed launch_workflow.py:68-74 waits for the original golden server to exit, beyond the production helper's own checks; this supports that particular golden restart but cannot repair the grading helper's general false-success path. library_flow.cjs:25-47 performs the actual save/reload/readback comparisons. Successful golden behavior therefore does not refute the resistant-process counterexample. These are direct scripted observations, not full configured judge, Oracle, target-model, or judge-duration measurements; none is claimed here.
counterexample: False-pass witness: a functioning playground uses server-memory records (or better-sqlite3(':memory:')) and installs a SIGTERM handler that leaves its listener alive. It can satisfy newly authored execution, real successful writes, independent-clean-context reads, reloads, revisions and subsequent saves. At S22 the inherited helper times out waiting for that original process to die, starts a replacement that exits with EADDRINUSE, then reports success because the original server still answers. Its untouched memory makes every exact persistence readback and later write appear successful, although a real completed process restart loses all records. The raw bound resistant-listener reproduction executed the false-success mechanism; the complete memory-backed playground and its resulting judge score were not executed. Conforming-alternative challenge: a local Express/SQLite app can use server-rendered library documents, arbitrary observed record field names/routes and no JSON list endpoint. The constraints wording explicitly accepts that design and the functional prompt discovers successful request shapes, so no false failure was found for that alternative.
suggested_fix: Escalate the canonical-template defect through an authorized shared-harness correction: report restart success only after bounded termination of the old process group and verified liveness of the replacement; otherwise return an explicit tool error. Then freeze a new candidate and verify both the resistant-process counterexample and normal durable read/write path. Do not silently patch this task's template-controlled files or claim a full judge result from scripted evidence.
